seed: A shape drawn with the Pen came out filled AND outlined in the one colour the Pen was armed with, so the outline was invisible and the painted shape reached half a line width past every point that was clicked: two points all round, which on a 24 point icon grid is a sixth of the drawing. A box stopped doing this in September. The walk draws a closed shape and checks it arrives as a fill and nothing else, asks for an edge and checks the edge it gets can actually be seen against that fill, then draws an open path and checks a line still comes out as a line.

steps.note: THE TEST: a closed shape off the Pen is its fill and nothing else. It used to arrive with 4 points of line painted the fill's own colour, so the panel claimed an outline the picture did not have and the shape sat 2 points bigger all round than the three points that were clicked.
THE TEST: the edge you ask for arrives in an ink that READS against the inside it sits on, not a second copy of the fill. The same rule a box's first border follows, so the two shapes behave alike.

THE TEST: an open path is untouched. A line IS its stroke, so a line of no width would not be a shape with no edge, it would be nothing at all: it comes out at the weight the canvas set and with no inside to paint.
